The proposed answer of 20 is incorrect. I recount the valid cells below.

A cell (i,j,k) can be red only if it is red in all three views: the top view S at (i,j), the front view M at (i,k), and the right view T at (j,k). The maximum is the number of such cells.

**Top layer (k = 5).**
- The top row of the front view is "+++++", so every i is allowed.
- The top row of the right view is "+++++", so every j is allowed.
- The only restriction comes from S. The rows of S have 5, 1, 5, 1, 5 red squares, which gives 17 cells.

**Layers k = 1 to 4.**
- The front view allows only i = 1, 3, 5.
- The right view allows only j = 3, the middle depth.
- The S row for j = 3 is "+++++", so all three of those cells are allowed.
- Each of the 4 layers therefore has 3 cells, giving 12 cells.

Flipping the depth direction does not change the count, because T is symmetric in j.

**Total:** 17 + 12 = 29.

The proposed solution put the full row of each view at k = 1, the bottom, instead of at the top. It also left out the whole top layer, where S allows 17 cells, so it undercounted.

The correct maximum is 29, not 20.

VERDICT: REJECT
